summary: Mission retries and approved revisions retain compatible completed work and bound person answers by reference; automatic supersession protects completed evidence and successors resolve the current launching-declaration workspace.

replay.detail: Existing carried references retain original completed evidence and person responses, including denials. A carried denial leaves the gate refused, never falsely completed. New asks record a typed continuity binding; historical unbound answers are not automatically adopted. No person answers or completion evidence are fabricated.

schema.detail: mission-run.gate-carried references original root decisions; optional claim fields record ask bindings, carried source attempts, and launching declaration workspace provenance. No storage table migration or client-v0 schema change.

rules.detail: Completed work and person responses prevent automatic supersession without existing explicit revision approval. Adoption checks step and dependency contracts, declared resolved inputs including head/ref values, requester and authority, and standing answer state. Human gate reuse tracks equivalent requests across runs, including unanswered candidates, so an original answer wakes dependent runs without polling. Revoking an old answer never resumes a different outstanding ask or makes the revoked answer reusable. Schedule and subscription successors resolve workspace from their current launching declaration.

compatibility.detail: Explicit API/CLI workspaces and historical runs without launch provenance retain their explicit workspace. Old unbound asks require explicit person-confirmed recovery; undeclared ambient repository heads are not inferred as consent bindings.

downtime.detail: No migration downtime. Ordinary upgrade activates native continuity handling.

manual.detail: Unchanged bound answers no longer require manual replay or a repeated launch ask. Historical unbound evidence requires one explicit authentic person confirmation.

recovery.detail: The native missions run continuity preview, recover, and startup-preview commands expose read-only eligibility and preview-hash-fenced recovery into a fresh linked run behind the ordinary cleanup fence.
